item.title: Microsoft: Azure API Management vulnerability used to steal credentials
item.description:
Microsoft: Azure API Management vulnerability used to steal credentials

Microsoft has issued a security advisory warning that a vulnerability in Azure API Management (APIM) Classic tiers was exploited to steal stored API credentials, with Norwegian authorities linking the flaw to cyberattacks against energy companies. The issue affects a cloud service that allows organizations to publish, secure, monitor, and manage APIs connecting applications, services, and data.

🔍 Overview

In a security advisory with Tracking ID MZK9-GH0, Microsoft stated it identified the vulnerability on November 18, 2026, and deployed a mitigation the following day. The company confirmed that customers were exposed and that an unauthorized party could have accessed secrets stored in Azure API Management Classic instances before the issue was identified.

⚙️ Key details

  • Affected Tiers: The vulnerability specifically affects Azure API Management Classic tiers; Microsoft stated that APIM v2 tiers are not impacted.
  • Access Mechanism: The flaw allowed unauthorized access to certain management functionality when APIM Classic instances were not configured according to recommended security best practices.
  • Potential Impact: This access could allow attackers to perform administrative operations, including accessing secrets, which could potentially grant access to additional applications, services, or backend systems depending on permissions.
  • Remediation: Microsoft closed the unauthorized access path on November 19 and rotated Microsoft-controlled keys and credentials where appropriate.
  • Limitation: The remediation does not automatically invalidate customer credentials that may have been accessed before the fix was deployed.

🏛️ Reported Exploitation

Norway’s National Security Authority (NSM) linked the vulnerability to attacks affecting Norwegian organizations, including energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi.

  • NSM Advisory: The agency stated that an unknown threat actor targeted access tokens, secrets, and named values stored in Azure API Management.
  • Discovery: NSM reported that Norway’s energy sector first discovered the vulnerability, noting that organizations in other countries and industries were also affected.
  • Equinor: The company disclosed an ongoing cyberattack on November 17, the day before Microsoft identified the vulnerability. Equinor later announced it had stopped the attack and found no indication that data had been stolen or altered.
  • Skagerak Energi: The company reported an attempted cyberattack but stated it had no impact on operations and no evidence that information was compromised.

Additionally, a Reddit post from an administrator alleged their organization detected unauthorized access to Azure Key Vault using a valid administrator token. The administrator claimed attackers exploited a zero-day authentication bypass in a deprecated legacy API to gain access to a privileged system account on APIM instances. They alleged the legacy API did not generate logs for customers to detect this access and that Microsoft initially attributed the activity to leaked customer credentials. BleepingComputer has not independently verified these allegations.

💡 Recommendations

Microsoft urged affected customers to:

  • Immediately rotate potentially exposed credentials.
  • Investigate suspicious activity in systems accessible through those credentials.
  • Review available logs for signs of unauthorized access.

NSM warned organizations to verify that their APIM instances have received the security update, noting that instances running below specific runtime versions remain vulnerable. The agency advised customers to contact their service provider if they have not received the update. Cloud security researcher Anders Kristiansen has shared threat-hunting queries to help organizations investigate potential exploitation and identify stored credentials.

#Azure #Cybersecurity #APIManagement #Vulnerability #Microsoft

Source: Microsoft Azure flaw exploited to steal customers’ API credentials

item.title: Unofficial Go Client for OpenAI API Supports Responses and GPT-6
item.description:
Unofficial Go Client for OpenAI API Supports Responses and GPT-6

An unofficial Go client for the OpenAI API is now available, providing support for both the new Responses API and legacy Chat Completions surfaces. The library requires Go 1.18 or later and covers a wide range of API capabilities including embeddings, images, audio, moderation, files, fine-tuning, batches, vector stores, and the legacy Assistants API.

🧩 How it works

For new integrations involving text generation, reasoning, tool-calling, or multi-turn interactions, the client recommends starting with the Responses API. Chat Completions remains available for existing integrations that specifically require its request or response shape. Developers using Azure OpenAI can utilize DefaultAzureConfig to configure deployment mapping or API versions required by their resources.

⚙️ Key details

  • Input Handling: Input can be defined as a string or a slice of typed input items.
  • Output Inspection: For reasoning, tools, multimodal output, or custom processing, developers should inspect response.Output rather than using the GetOutputText convenience method.
  • Context Management: PreviousResponseID is used to carry earlier response context, while Instructions must be resent on each call to ensure they continue to apply.
  • Model IDs: Accepted as strings, allowing the use of models before named constants are added to the package.
  • Error Handling: API failures can be inspected using errors.As.

📊 Model Support

The client supports specific reasoning effort levels for GPT-6 models. GPT-6 models generally support low, medium (default), high, xhigh, and max reasoning. Additionally, GPT-6.1 Terra, GPT-6 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna support none. Tool calling via Responses is supported for GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6.2 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6 Astra. Chat Completions function calling with reasoning_effort set to none is supported for GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna.

💡 Why it matters

This client allows Go developers to integrate with the latest OpenAI features, including advanced reasoning and agent-driven workflows. It also promotes Unreal Agent, a Go-based, fully async harness designed to drive cost savings compared to Codex.

#Go #OpenAI #API #GPT-6 #DeveloperTools

Source: sashabaranov/go-openai

item.title: Tencent APIJSON demo projects support multiple languages and frameworks
item.description:
Tencent APIJSON demo projects support multiple languages and frameworks

Tencent has published demo projects for APIJSON, featuring usage examples, documentation, and test data SQL files for various programming languages, frameworks, and clients.

🔍 Overview

The project provides sample code and resources for different environments, including:

  • Languages: Java, Swift, JavaScript, Python, and others.
  • Frameworks: SpringBoot, JFinal, and others.
  • Clients: Web, Android, iOS, and others.

🧩 How it works

The demo suite includes automated testing tools such as APIAuto, UnitAuto, SQLAuto, AutoUI, and CVAuto. These tools support simple demo apps for testing APIJSON as well as complex production apps like social media feeds.

⚙️ Key details

  • Server Testing: Users can test API endpoints by skipping setup and using the APIJSON official server address apijson.cn:8080.
  • Tools: Developers can use the APIAuto machine learning HTTP interface tool or download client Apps for testing.
  • Client Libraries: Documentation and links are available for Android, iOS, and JavaScript clients.
  • Support: Questions can be submitted as issues on the APIJSON core project.

🚀 Availability

The APIJSON-Demo repository is available on GitHub. The project lists contributors including two Tencent engineers, one ByteDance engineer, one Ping An Technology engineer, and the author of the Solon framework.

#APIJSON #Tencent #GitHub #Programming #Testing

Source: APIJSON/APIJSON-Demo

item.title: Hayhooks deploys AI agents and pipelines as REST and MCP endpoints
item.description:
Hayhooks deploys AI agents and pipelines as REST and MCP endpoints

Hayhooks allows developers to deploy Python wrappers or YAML pipelines as typed, validated endpoints, supporting REST APIs, OpenAI-compatible chat, MCP tools, and A2A agents with durable execution and built-in tracing.

🧩 How it works

  • Endpoint Generation: Deployments use method type hints to validate requests and generate the API schema.
  • Protocol Support: The system supports REST APIs, OpenAI-compatible chat completions, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, and Agent2Agent (A2A) agents.
  • UI Integration: Users can connect Open WebUI or use the embedded Chainlit UI to chat with agents.

⚙️ Key details

  • Streaming & Responses: Serves streaming Chat Completions and Responses endpoints, with responses arriving as server-sent events.
  • Durable Execution: Long-running work is checkpointed in Redis, allowing the system to wait for human approval, retry failures, and recover after restarts.
  • Observability: Executions and component traces can be inspected in a terminal dashboard or exported to an OpenTelemetry backend using hayhooks[tracing].
  • MCP & A2A Capabilities: Runs an MCP server that exposes pipelines and agents as tools for Cursor, Claude Desktop, and other clients. Exposes chat-capable pipelines through the Agent2Agent protocol with generated agent cards for discovery and task delegation.

🚀 Availability

  • Requirements: Python 3.10 through 3.14 and an OpenAI API key are required.
  • Access: API docs are available at http://localhost:1416/docs for inspection and testing.

#Hayhooks #MCP #RESTAPI #AIAgents #Observability

Source: deepset-ai/hayhooks

item.title: Langfuse CLI v4 released with new commands and API versioning
item.description:
Langfuse CLI v4 released with new commands and API versioning

Langfuse has released a new CLI tool, @langfuse/cli, which allows users to interact with the Langfuse API directly from the command line. This new release includes updates to command aliases, input handling for complex JSON structures, and specific versioning rules for self-hosted versus cloud deployments.

📦 Package details

  • Package name: @langfuse/cli
  • Executable: langfuse
  • Legacy name: Previously published under langfuse-cli; the new name is recommended for all future use.

⚙️ Configuration and Host Selection

The CLI does not automatically read .env files. Users must manually configure API access and host selection. Host selection follows a specific priority order:

Priority Configuration Method
1 LANGFUSE_BASE_URL
2 LANGFUSE_HOST
3 EU default

To authenticate, users create a project API key pair under Project settings → API Keys.

🧩 Command and Input Features

  • Lossless input: --body-json and --body-file flags provide a lossless input path for nested objects, arrays, unions, and free-form JSON.
  • Pagination: The CLI can fetch every page of a paginated list, supporting both page- and cursor-based endpoints, with a maximum of 1000 items.
  • Aliases: OpenAPI tags and explicit route versions remain accepted aliases (e.g., scores-v3 list for the canonical scores list).
  • Schema: Verbose OpenAPI operationId values are available in api schema --json but are never required as CLI commands.

🌐 Availability and Versioning

  • V3 API Snapshots: Available on self-hosted deployments only.
  • Langfuse Cloud: Supports v4 and up.
  • Backward Compatibility: Users can use an API snapshot compatible with an older self-hosted deployment.

#Langfuse #CLI #API #DeveloperTools

Source: langfuse/langfuse-cli

item.title: Python SDK for Model Context Protocol Released
item.description:
Python SDK for Model Context Protocol Released

The official Python SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients has been released, providing a Python implementation of the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The documentation is available at https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/, including a Get started guide, What’s new in v2, the API reference, and a migration guide.

🔍 Overview

  • The Model Context Protocol lets you build servers that expose data and functionality to LLM applications in a secure, standardized way.
  • Think of it like a web API, but designed for LLM interactions.

🧩 How it works

  • Build MCP servers that expose tools, resources, and prompts to any MCP host.
  • Build MCP clients that connect to any MCP server.
  • Speak every standard transport: stdio, Streamable HTTP, and SSE.
  • Python 3.11+ is required.

⚙️ Key details

  • The cli extra adds the mcp command-line tool (mcp dev, mcp run, mcp install) on top of the SDK; install plain mcp if you don’t need it.
  • For one-off commands, uv run --with "mcp[cli]" mcp ... works without a project.
  • Example usage: Add two numbers or greet someone by name.
  • That’s a complete MCP server: one tool, one templated resource.
  • Call add with a=1, b=2 and you get 3 back.
  • Notice what you did not write: no JSON Schema (a: int, b: int is the schema), no request parsing, no validation code, no protocol handling.
  • Two type-hinted Python functions and a docstring.
  • The same package is a full MCP client.
  • A URL means Streamable HTTP, the transport you deploy.
  • Client can also launch a local server as a stdio subprocess or take any custom transport.

🚀 Availability

  • The project is licensed under the MIT License.
  • Contributions are welcome; see the contributing guide to get started.

💡 Why it matters

  • The SDK simplifies building and connecting to MCP servers and clients, reducing the need for manual request parsing, validation, and protocol handling.
  • It supports various transports, making it versatile for different deployment scenarios.
  • The project aims to support contributors of all levels of experience.

#PythonSDK #ModelContextProtocol #LLMApplications #AITools

Source: modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk

item.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro launches on Moonshot API with competitive pricing and strong benchmark scores
item.description:
Kimi K3.1 Pro launches on Moonshot API with competitive pricing and strong benchmark scores

Kimi K3.1 Pro landed on the Kimi API today. The model is not yet available with open weights, but Moonshot has promised full weight release by November 4, 2026.

🔍 Overview

  • Kimi K3.1 Pro is the latest offering from Moonshot and is positioned alongside leading frontier models such as Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT‑6 Astra.
  • An “Highspeed” variant is also announced, delivering 2–3× faster inference at twice the price (input‑token‑cache‑hit pricing remains unchanged).

⚙️ Key details

  • Open‑weight timeline: Full model weights slated for release on 2026‑11‑04.
  • Pricing (USD):
    • Input tokens: $2.00 per million tokens
    • Output tokens: $10.00 per million tokens
    • Pricing matches GPT‑6.1 Sol and is half the cost of Claude Opus 5.5.
  • Model variants:
    • Standard Kimi K3.1 Pro
    • Highspeed version (2–3× faster, double price except for cached input tokens)

📈 Benchmarks

  • Moonshot’s internal benchmarks place Kimi K3.1 Pro roughly on par with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT‑6 Astra, beating them on a few tests and coming close on others.
  • Independent scoring by Artificial Analysis gives Kimi a score of 55, ahead of:
    • Claude Fable 5.1 – 53
    • GPT‑6 Astra – 53
    • Gemini 4 Argon – 53
    • and behind Claude Opus 5.5 – 58.
  • This is the first time a soon‑to‑be open‑weight model has scored this highly against the current frontier.
Model Score
Claude Opus 5.5 58
Kimi K3.1 Pro 55
Claude Fable 5.1 53
GPT‑6 Astra 53
Gemini 4 Argon 53

🛠️ How to use

The model can be accessed via the Moonshot API using an OpenAI‑compatible endpoint. Example command (run with the llm tool version 0.32):

llm openai endpoint \
 https://api.moonshot.ai/v1 \
 --key kimi \
 -m kimi-k3.1-pro \
 "Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle" \
 --responses \
 -o reasoning_effort low \
 > kimi-k3.1-pro-pelican-low.stdout.txt \
 2> kimi-k3.1-pro-pelican-low.stderr.txt

The endpoint supports three reasoning levels—low, medium, and max—producing different “pelican” outputs for each level.

🚀 Availability

  • Kimi K3.1 Pro is now live on the Kimi API.
  • Open weights are not yet released; the promised date is November 4, 2026.
  • The Highspeed version will be priced at twice the standard rate, with the exception that input‑token‑cache‑hit pricing stays the same.

item.title: OpenAI launches Decisions API with image‑capable decision model
item.description:
OpenAI launches Decisions API with image‑capable decision model

OpenAI released its new Decisions API, a Jev‑style service announced at last week’s DevDay.

🔍 Overview

  • The Decisions API follows the same conceptual shape as the existing Jev service.
  • Announced during OpenAI’s DevDay.

🧩 How it works

  • Supports three question types: yes/no, multiple‑choice, and scoring.
  • Accepts text input; the gpt‑6‑luna decision model also accepts image input.
  • Charges are applied only to input tokens.

⚙️ Key details

  • Pricing: 10 ¢ per million input tokens for OpenAI; Jev charges 4.2 ¢ per million input tokens.
  • No fee for output tokens.
  • A plugin (llm‑openai‑decisions) can be installed; the README shows the install command.
  • The README includes an example query against an image attachment and the corresponding example output.

🚀 Availability

  • The service was announced at last week’s DevDay and is available via the new plugin.

#OpenAI #DecisionsAPI #LLM #ImageInput #Pricing

Source: Release: llm-openai-decisions 0.1a0
